comment: Allowed under LIM-0019.
Fits only through the roaming element, as the note says. A regional agreement secured by the Commission is not alignment of national law; no better issue exists. Taxonomy gap for G5.
MKD-CIRT statistics on hacked sites, not cybercrime enforcement statistics, so in scope.
The quote only reports that the strategy was developed with EC support; it gives no specific support for RI-TEC-020 or RI-TEC-018, though the strategy covers those subjects.
"Has still not been built" reads as a finding or barrier, not an intervention, which would make the link unresolved_gap. The fit to RI-TEC-001 is also thin, as the note admits.
The quote also calls for full autonomy and independence in managing human resources; MKD-GOV-2026-002-0085 on the same point carries MEC-05.
Roaming glide path, read from the preceding items; same stretched fit to RI-TEC-011 as other regional roaming items. Taxonomy gap for G5.

Extraction note says this rates a sub-area, not a whole chapter, so the note is inexact. The evidence file, changed at 09:36 after this sample was drawn at 09:35, now already has RI-TEC-017. The sample value was reviewed.
EU-promoted regional initiative across many sectors, with nothing specific to the country; RI-TEC-033 is only the nearest fit, as the note says.

General participation in the Digital Agenda for connectivity and interoperability; no national targets, plans or investment as in RI-TEC-014. Sits in the infrastructure section, so RI-TEC-014 is defensible.
Same stretched fit to RI-TEC-011 for the regional roaming agreement; the Digital Agenda reference supports RI-TEC-002 only weakly.

The barrier concerns interruption of the interoperability platform through a lack of IT staff. No cybersecurity element in the item or its neighbours, and the only theme is TECH-INTEROP; RI-TEC-023 concerns exposure to attacks.
Section shows the Central Register is the point of single contact, so RI-TEC-007 fits.
Not a rating, so the G4-D09 note is inexact. A general statement in a literature passage about regional labour mobility, with no link to EU workers in the country; the chapter basis is doubtful.
The quote says understaffing undermines the ability to act independently; MEC-05 is reasonable as well as MEC-03.
Chapter 10 rating, accepted under G4-D09. The same sentence is also extracted as an intervention (-0081), which carries the law.
A budget subtotal ("Sub-area 2 TOTAL"), not a rating, so the G4-D09 note is false. A theme item with no issue fails the scope check in rules section 5 and should not be auto.
Same sentence is also extracted as a metric (-0013); the figure is regional.
Regional cooperation by the authority does not show lack of independence or resources; RI-TEC-018 is only the closest fit, as the note says.
What remains to be done is NIS2 legislation, so RI-TEC-022 is the better first issue under "best fit first". Both issues are right.
Undefined web services and user roles are an access-control weakness on the platform, but RI-TEC-023 concerns incident response staff and secure infrastructure, so the fit is weak.
Section is the strategic goal on the authority's independence, which supports RI-TEC-018.
The quote speaks of alignment through the two laws; RI-TEC-018 has support only from the strategy goal elsewhere, not from this passage.

Message counts in counter-terrorism cooperation show use of SIENA, not a readiness gap; technology is barely the subject. The extraction note applies R22 consistently with two other items, so not clearly wrong. Worth a G5 ruling.
Section is the e-archiving reform step, so RI-TEC-004 fits although the quote alone is bare.
Monitoring of alignment with the digitalisation laws fits RI-TEC-002; the note itself says the RI-TEC-003 definition does not clearly cover this.
IT post vacancies; the next item links them to absent security certification, which gives RI-TEC-023 some support, but the quote itself has no security element.
Departure from the default chain link is explained in the note, as rules section 1 allows.
